# Data Model and Data Entry: Overview

This document provides an overview of the data model and data entry templates for the research database on sexual abuse in the Swiss Catholic Church.

## Architecture

The database separates **data model** (persistent structure) from **data entry** (UI/forms), enabling independent evolution of structure and interface.

> **Single Source of Truth**: Detailed schema definitions are maintained in `data/schemas/`. This document provides a high-level overview with links to detailed specifications.

## Directory Structure

``` text
data/
├── schemas/              # Entity schemas and data model
│   ├── *-schema.md      # Entity definitions
│   ├── erm-diagram.qmd  # Relationships
│   ├── edtf-documentation.md
│   └── vocabularies/    # Controlled terms
└── templates/           # MediaWiki templates and forms
    ├── Vorlage_*.xml    # Display templates
    ├── Formular_*.xml   # Entry forms
    └── Kategorie_*.xml  # Cargo declarations
```

```{mermaid}
%% === Relationships ===

Fall --> Betroffener : Betroffener
Fall --> Beschuldigter : Beschuldigter
Fall --> Kirchliche_Institution : Institutioneller_Kontext

Beschuldigter --> Kirchliche_Institution : Institutioneller_Kontext

```

### 1. FALL (Case)

Central entity representing individual abuse cases with timeline, source criticism score, institutional response, and legal proceedings.

**Schema**: [faelle-schema.md](../data/schemas/faelle-schema.md)

### 2. BETROFFENER (Affected Person)

Pseudonymized victims/survivors with demographics, contact status, and institutional relationships.

**Schema**: [betroffene-schema.md](../data/schemas/betroffene-schema.md)

### 3. BESCHULDIGTER (Accused Person)

Accused individuals (clergy, employees, volunteers) with clerical roles, institutional affiliations, and transfer history.

**Schema**: [beschuldigte-schema.md](../data/schemas/beschuldigte-schema.md)

### 4. KIRCHLICHE_INSTITUTION (Church Institution)

Churches, schools, homes, religious orders with type, location, and diocese/order affiliation.

**Schema**: [kirchliche-institutionen-schema.md](../data/schemas/kirchliche-institutionen-schema.md)

### 5. STRAFVERFOLGUNGSBEHOERDE (Law Enforcement)

Prosecuting authorities and victim support services with type, jurisdiction, and area of responsibility.

**Schema**: [strafverfolgungsbehoerden-schema.md](../data/schemas/strafverfolgungsbehoerden-schema.md)

### 6. FACHGREMIUM (Expert Committee)

Review boards, commissions, advisory panels with type, mandate, and composition.

**Schema**: [fachgremien-schema.md](../data/schemas/fachgremien-schema.md)

## Entity Relationships

See detailed diagram: [erm-diagram.qmd](../data/schemas/erm-diagram.qmd)

-   Cases link to affected persons, accused persons, institutions, authorities, and committees
-   Many-to-many relationships enable tracking of institutional transfers and multi-entity cases

## EDTF Date Handling

The project uses **Extended Date/Time Format (EDTF)** for uncertain (`1985?`), approximate (`1985~`), partial (`1985`), and range (`1985/1990`) dates. This accommodates incomplete records and protects privacy.

**Documentation**: [edtf-documentation.md](../data/schemas/edtf-documentation.md)

## Data Entry Templates

**Location**: [data/templates/](../data/templates/)

Three template types define data entry:

1.  **Vorlagen (Display)** - Format entity pages and store to Cargo
2.  **Formulare (Forms)** - Interactive entry with validation and controlled vocabularies
3.  **Kategorien (Categories)** - Cargo table structure and category membership

See [Templates documentation](../data/templates/index.qmd) for details.

## Privacy and Ethics

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: This repository documents structure only. Real research data is stored in **ETH Zürich LeoMed** secure infrastructure under GDPR/DSGVO and research ethics protocols.

## Research Significance

Enables pattern detection (transfers, geographic distribution), quantitative analysis (source criticism, timelines), cross-language harmonization (German/French/Italian), and methodological innovation (operationalizing source criticism).

## Technical Stack

-   **Database**: Semantic MediaWiki + Cargo + Page Forms
-   **Analysis**: Python, R, Jupyter (scripts in `src/` and `analysis/`)
-   **Version Control**: Git/GitHub

## Workflow

**Template Developers**: Review schemas → Create templates/forms → Define Cargo tables → Export XML

**Data Entry**: Login → Navigate to `Special:FormStart/[EntityType]` → Fill form → Save to Cargo

**Analysts**: Query Cargo → Export → Process in Python → Analyze → Visualize → Document

## Versioning

Schemas use Semantic Versioning (MAJOR: breaking changes, MINOR: add fields, PATCH: documentation). Vocabularies versioned separately. Changes documented in CHANGELOG.

## Quality Assurance

**Validation**: PageForms (entry) → Cargo (storage) → Python scripts (schemas) → Human review

**Metrics**: Completeness, consistency, source quality, relationship integrity
